name: שְׁמַרְיָה
summary: Four men: one of the Benjamites, Saul's kin, who came to David at Ziklag (1Ch 12:6, in the long form שְׁמַרְיָהוּ); a son of Rehoboam by Mahalath (2Ch 11:19); and two men of Ezra's day who had taken foreign wives, of the sons of Harim and of Bani (Ezr 10:32, 41). The name is the perfect of שָׁמַר with the divine name: “Yahweh has kept”, the confession of Psalm 121, “Yahweh is your keeper”. Scripture does not comment on the name.

evidence.note: Among those who came to David at Ziklag: “Eluzai and Jerimoth and Bealiah וּשְׁמַרְיָהוּ and Shephatiah the Haruphite”.
Rehoboam's wife “bore him sons: Jeush and שְׁמַרְיָה and Zaham”.
The name as a sentence: יַהְוֶה שֹׁמְרֶךָ, “Yahweh is your keeper”.
The verb of the name, of Yahweh: וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ, “I will keep you wherever you go”.

note: 1Ch 12:6 is 12:5 in English numbering (TIPNR key Shemariah@1Ch.12.5). Punic ŠMRBʿL, “Baal protect” (Krahmalkov p. 470), is the same kind of name with another god.
